App details

Device Info & Diagnostics

Explore your phone’s hardware and system information, and run simple checks.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

Browse hardware, system, battery, display, camera and sensor information, run selected live checks and share a privacy-filtered TXT or JSON report.

Main features

  • Battery, storage, screen, camera and sensor details.
  • Touch, display, audio and live sensor checks.
  • Copy information or share a text or JSON report.
  • Reports omit sensitive device identifiers.

This app is being planned and is not yet available to download. The description presents its intended functions.

Features in detail

Device information and individual checks

Overview and detailed device information

Open the overview for model, Android, memory, storage, display and battery, then explore detailed pages. See processor architecture/core count, graphics chip, total/available RAM, total/free/used storage, display resolution/density/refresh/HDR, and battery charge/state/source/temperature/voltage where reported. Missing or restricted fields are labelled rather than guessed.

Motion, magnetism and inclination tests

Select a sensor instance and start a live test. Accelerometer and gyroscope show three-axis values and short graphs while you move the phone. The magnetometer shows X/Y/Z components and field magnitude; orientation/inclination shows response to tilting. These observations do not certify the sensor’s accuracy.

Light, proximity and pressure tests

Cover or expose the light sensor to watch lux values change. Bring an object near the proximity sensor to see near/far or the actual reported distance. A pressure sensor shows hPa and a short graph. The app does not invent centimetres for a binary sensor or turn pressure into a weather forecast.

Touchscreen, pixels, vibration and flashlight

Touch the screen to mark areas and see simultaneous touch points. Inspect full-screen colour/brightness patterns for dead or stuck pixels. Trigger vibration or a supported flashlight and judge the result yourself. Separate lights are selectable when the device exposes them; a visual test is not an automatic hardware certificate.

Camera, microphone and audio-output checks

Choose an available camera for preview with permission; camera capabilities can be viewed without starting preview. Select an exposed microphone to see live level and a short waveform, with no saved recording. Play test sound and left/right channels on supported outputs, then give your own verdict. Each separately accessible device has its own result.

Network state and supported features

See the active connection type and reported internet, metered or validated status, plus features the Android system declares. These indicators explain availability, not a network scan or proof that every declared feature works. Unavailable information remains clearly marked.

Copy, text/JSON report and sharing

Copy relevant fields or export a readable text report or structured JSON file, then share through Android. Reports keep separate device instances but omit stable unique identifiers, SIM information and IP address by default. Nothing uploads automatically; you choose the recipient or file location.

What a diagnostic result means

Tests are user-started and can succeed, fail, be unavailable or remain inconclusive. A success applies to the checked function only; visual, sound and vibration checks need your judgment. This tool shows available information and responses, not automatic certification of the whole phone or a battery-health percentage guessed from basic readings.

An overly thorough check

Tap the About logo seven times for a fictional checklist that finishes by detecting the user. The offline joke does not run real hardware tests or change diagnostic results. Close it to return to the normal app.

Use, settings and availability

Offline use

The main functions are designed to work on your device without a JN86 account. Ads, purchases and external links may need internet.

Language, settings and help

Choose one of eight app languages and adjust the available settings. About provides privacy information and a link to voluntary JN86 support. Support does not unlock paid functions. Availability is shown below.

Ads and optional ad removal

All described functions are planned to be free, with banner ads and optional one-time Google Play ad removal. No subscription is planned. The purchase screen shows the actual local price; purchase restoration uses Google Play.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
